- **18 an Dàmhair, LE 1,519** — *Baile Mòr ruadh's fair* (Baile Mòr ruadh). Baile Mòr ruadh in the east holds a cattle fair that draws drovers from Àth chiar and the eastern hills. It becomes yearly, and the greatest fair in the east.
- **9 an t-Iuchar, LE 1,529** — *Queen Sìleas Òg crowned* (Cathair dhearg). Sìleas Òg of Clann Raghnaill, named for the queen of the firlot, is crowned at Cathair dhearg. She is the first ruler known to have visited every shire seat.
- **4 an Dàmhair, LE 1,539** — *Sìleas Òg's count of hands* (Muileann dhearg). Queen Sìleas Òg commands a new count of every household holding the right to the coal. It is smaller than any before, for the right has narrowed into fewer and larger households, and the queen has it entered without comment.
- **5 an t-Sultain, LE 1,549** — *The fire of Ceann mhin* (Ceann mhin). A second great fire burns Ceann mhin, and this time there is no war to blame. By order of its reeve the town is rebuilt with gable walls of stone between the houses.
- **31 an Lùnastal, LE 1,559** — *The silver smelt refused* (Muileann chiar — baile mèinne airgid). Clann Choinnich asks leave to burn the coal beyond the measured handful to smelt silver at Muileann chiar, since the coal burns hotter than charcoal. The council refuses. It is the first asking to burn the coal for work and not for worship.
- **22 an t-Ògmhios, LE 1,569** — *The lost smithing at Dùn dhearg* (Dùn dhearg). The smiths of Dùn dhearg, makers of the ceremonial blades of the custodian houses since the walls were built, lose the last man who knew how their layered steel was folded. After him the blades of Dùn dhearg are ordinary.
- **2 an Dùbhlachd, LE 1,579** — *The houses bury at Tuam Cnoc dhìreach* (Tuam Cnoc dhìreach). The custodian houses begin to bury their heads at Tuam Cnoc dhìreach, among graves older than any name on them. The tenants of the land about call it unwise, and go on burying their own dead elsewhere.
- **9 an t-Iuchar, LE 1,589** — *King Ailean the Fourth crowned* (Cathair dhearg). Ailean mac Raghnaill, fourth king of that name, is crowned at Cathair dhearg. He is remembered only for the shortest reign in the king-list.
- **13 an Giblean, LE 1,590** — *The synod of Manannan's order* (Seann Skell). The priests of Manannan meet at Seann Skell and lay down again the rule of sight-of-land. To it they add a prayer, said at the foot of the river pool, that Manannan keep the sea shut: A Mhanannain, cùm a' mhuir dùinte.
- **12 an Cèitean, LE 1,590** — *Queen Mòrag nic Ailein crowned* (Cathair dhearg). Ailean's sister Mòrag nic Ailein is crowned after him. She reigns forty years, and the king-list has for her its longest run of entries telling of nothing but good harvests and the rite.
- **16 an t-Samhain, LE 1,619** — *The ferry at Cidhe Beag* (Cidhe Beag). A ferry family settles at Cidhe Beag on Abhainn uaine and carries folk and goods down the river by canoe. They hold the landing for the rest of the age.
- **1 an Dàmhair, LE 1,626** — *The dark wine of Àth shean* (Àth shean). The growers on the slopes above Àth shean press blaeberry and bramble into a dark wine that keeps a year in the cask. It is sold along the eastern road, and the road-houses serve it as black wine.
- **2 an t-Samhain, LE 1,634** — *Inis mhòr's grain fleet laid up* (Inis mhòr). The coasting grain barges of Inis mhòr, which had sailed Slighe-uisce fhuar, the cold way along the north coast from Ros chiar to Caol mhin, since the Holy Age, are laid up for good as the roads grow better. The last is kept on the strand as a wonder.
- **7 an Lùnastal, LE 1,649** — *Earthquake at Dùn ìseal* (Dùn ìseal). An earthquake shakes Dùn ìseal and cracks the spirit-house. No one is killed. The keepers take it for a warning, but cannot agree of what.
- **21 an Cèitean, LE 1,659** — *Beathag nic Thòmais gathers the old copies* (Muileann chaol). Beathag nic Thòmais, widow of a mill-owner of Muileann chaol, begins to buy old copies of the custody-book and the harbour rolls from houses that no longer read them. She keeps them in a loft over her mill.
- **28 am Faoilleach, LE 1,674** — *The paper mill at Muileann chaol* (Muileann chaol). A mill at Muileann chaol begins to make paper from rags, the first on Dia-thìr. In this generation the custody-book is first copied onto paper.
- **27 an Giblean, LE 1,679** — *Three copies of the landfall tidings* (Muileann chaol). Among her papers Beathag nic Thòmais finds three copies of the tidings of the two landfalls. They differ in the order of the coasts and the number of hulls. She writes out all three side by side and does not choose between them.
- **3 an Cèitean, LE 1,694** — *The north-west coast counted* (Baile chrom). The crown sends a reeve to list the households of the thinned north-west coast between Baile chrom and Ceann mhòr. He counts fewer households than there are harbour berths.
- **24 an Lùnastal, LE 1,699** — *The loft at Muileann chaol* (Muileann chaol). Beathag nic Thòmais dies, and leaves her loft of papers to the town of Muileann chaol on condition that nothing in it be burned. The town keeps that condition and very little else of her wishes.
- **6 am Màrt, LE 1,709** — *King Tormod mac Ruairidh crowned* (Cathair dhearg). Tormod mac Ruairidh of Clann Raghnaill is crowned at Cathair dhearg. His reign is remembered for its roads and its length.
- **5 an Gearran, LE 1,714** — *Manannan's harbour prayer* (Seann Skell). The priests of Manannan at Seann Skell begin to say their prayer for the shut sea on the day of the rite of the empty harbour, so that both are kept together on Cidhe an Diosail. Neither side is pleased.
- **6 am Màrt, LE 1,719** — *Tormod's bridges* (Cnoc ìseal). King Tormod builds stone bridges over the fords of the south-central shires, one of them at Cnoc ìseal. Ferry-keepers who lose their living are given land in amends.
- **9 an Dùbhlachd, LE 1,729** — *The panther year* (Imrich nam Pantar). The panthers cross the southern roads in numbers beyond any herder's memory, and for a whole season the crossing days run into one another. Flocks are kept in folds from Cnoc àrsaidh to the coast.
- **10 an t-Samhain, LE 1,734** — *Caol gharbh loses the salt* (Caol gharbh). The sea rises over the salt pans of Caol gharbh and they fail, and salt comes to the north-east from the south instead. The town that took the trade of Ros fhionn is poorer than Ros fhionn had been.
- **12 an Dàmhair, LE 1,739** — *Storm at Baile ghorm* (Baile ghorm). A south-westerly storm floods the low town of Baile ghorm and drowns twenty-three. The town raises its sea-wall by the height of a man.
- **22 an Cèitean, LE 1,749** — *The rite kept by few* (Seann Skell). The rite of the empty harbour on Cidhe an Diosail at Seann Skell is kept by the harbour priests and a few old families. A visiting scribe writes that none there could say on what day the fleet had in truth sailed.
- **23 an Giblean, LE 1,754** — *Cuan dhearg flooded again* (Cuan dhearg). The sea comes over the waterfront of Cuan dhearg a second time, and the street moved back after An Gàire Dubh is flooded to the thresholds. The town builds a sea-wall and does not move again.
- **20 an Giblean, LE 1,759** — *The house at Dùn thais reopened* (Dùn thais). The house of disputation at Dùn thais, shut and opened more than once since the table of years, is opened again on condition that the question of longer lives is not raised. The druids of the schools accept it and argue about the vein instead.
- **9 an Dùbhlachd, LE 1,766** — *Death of King Tormod* (Cathair dhearg). King Tormod mac Ruairidh dies at Cathair dhearg after a reign of more than fifty years. His daughter Gormshuil nic Thormoid is crowned.
- **12 an Giblean, LE 1,771** — *Queen Gormshuil's progress* (Cathair dhearg). Queen Gormshuil nic Thormoid rides round every shire seat of the island, the first ruler to do so since Sìleas Òg. Her clerks write down the grievances of each shire; the queen answers none of them in writing.
- **5 an Gearran, LE 1,776** — *The second silver petition* (Muileann dhearg). Clann Choinnich asks again to burn the coal beyond the measure for the silver smelt at Muileann chiar, now with three of the seven houses behind it. Queen Gormshuil's council refuses by one voice. The name of the member who changed his vote is written down; his reason is not.
- **25 am Màrt, LE 1,786** — *An Taigh-òsta Grianach's spinach* (An Taigh-òsta Grianach). An Taigh-òsta Grianach on the eastern road feeds the queen's progress with pan-fried spinach and black wine, as the charter-roll records. Its keeper, Peigi nic Dhonnchaidh, is spared her road dues for a year.
- **27 an Gearran, LE 1,791** — *The last count of hands* (Muileann dhearg). The vein-house counts for the last time in this age the households holding the right to the coal. They are fewer than at any count before, and greater; the custody-book notes that three of the seven houses now hold more than half the right between them.
- **22 an Cèitean, LE 1,794** — *Timber from the west* (Ceann mhòr). A worked timber, longer than any tree on the island and fastened with nails of a make no smith of Dia-thìr knows, comes ashore at Ceann mhòr on the north-west coast, from beyond Manannan's mist, as the fishers say. It is carried to Seann Skell, shown to Manannan's priests, and burned.
- **24 an Dàmhair, LE 1,799** — *The lamps at Seann Skell go out* (Seann Skell). Fewer houses at Seann Skell keep the night of lamps each year, and at last none on the waterfront. An old woman sets a lamp in a window of the harbour-house, and the scribe writes that it was she and not the town.
- **25 an t-Samhain, LE 1,803** — *The last rite of the empty harbour in this age* (Seann Skell). Eleven people keep the rite of the empty harbour at Seann Skell. The harbour scribe enters their number, the weather and the state of the tide, and nothing more.
- **28 an Dùbhlachd, LE 1,806** — *The silver petition laid aside* (Muileann chiar — baile mèinne airgid). The member who had turned the vote being dead, Clann Choinnich does not bring its silver petition to the council again. It lies unanswered in the vein-house, and the age ends with the Small-Burning Law still kept.
- **27 an Dàmhair, LE 1,813** — *The mist thins* (Seann Skell). The priests of Manannan at Seann Skell write that the mist on the western sea, which has hidden Dia-thìr from every ship beyond it since the fleet of the Sundering sailed into it, lies thinner each winter. They say their prayer, A Mhanannain, cùm a' mhuir dùinte, at every tide, and on still mornings the fishers of the west coast begin to see the line of the open sea beyond the headlands.

## Age IV · An Aois Choigreach

*The Age of Strangers · the Anchor Era, AE 1 – 151*

- **5 am Faoilleach, AE 1** — *The Crossing*. Humans come ashore on Dia-thìr, bringing their Church with them, and are given leave to stay. They are the first strangers met since the Sundering.
- **13 am Faoilleach, AE 1** — *The ships met off the north-west* (Coinneachadh nan Long). That winter the mist that had lain on the western sea since the fleet of the Sundering sailed into it lifts. Two fishing boats of Achadh àrsaidh, working the water off the north-west cape where the Sea-Watcher is seen, meet three ships coming out of the thin grey from the west, and hail them; neither side understands the other. The fishers turn south and the ships follow them down the coast toward Cuan shean. The fishers call the place Coinneachadh nan Long, the meeting of the ships, and the boats of Achadh àrsaidh still slow there.
- **5 an Gearran, AE 1** — *Three ships off Cuan shean* (Cuan shean). Three ships out of the west anchor off Cuan shean, the first hulls of their size seen from Dia-thìr since the fleet of the Sundering. Their master, a captain the rolls name Edmund Harrow, comes ashore unarmed with eleven men and asks by signs for water.
- **16 an t-Ògmhios, AE 1** — *Forty days on the dunes* (Cuan shean). The custodians of Cuan shean will not decide alone, and send inland to the capital for counsel. For forty days the strangers are fed on the beach and kept below the dunes.
- **10 an t-Iuchar, AE 1** — *The custodian of Baile fhiadhaich rides south* (Baile fhiadhaich). Word of the ships reaches Baile fhiadhaich, up the western coast, in three days. Its custodian rides south to see them, and writes to the council that the strangers' ropes are better than ours and their manners worse.
- **11 am Faoilleach, AE 2** — *The Council of Custodians grants leave* (Cathair dhearg). The Council of Custodians at Cathair dhearg, which has sat in the crown's place since the crown fell empty at the close of the Age of Sundering, confirms the strangers' leave to stay under the high custodian Tormod mac Ailein. The council roll gives the vote as with one voice; a later hand in the margin notes that three custodians were absent.
- **9 an Gearran, AE 2** — *The quarter of sea they came from* (Cuan shean). Old sailors at Cuan shean say that the strangers came in from the same quarter of sea the fleet of the Sundering sailed into. The council forbids the saying in its hall. It is written down all the same, and never answered.
- **26 an Gearran, AE 2** — *The land beyond*. The strangers name their homeland in their own tongue, but no scribe of the Dia-thìrich writes the word down. From the first season the scribes call it an Tìr Thall, the land beyond, and its people simply the humans.
- **27 am Màrt, AE 2** — *The first attempts at speech*. For a whole season clerics of the humans' Church and custodians of Dia-thìr labour to make a store of words in common. Neither side's account of what was agreed survives whole.
- **13 an Dùbhlachd, AE 2** — *Wren's word-lists* (Cathair dhearg). The human cleric Samuel Wren and the custodian Gormshuil nic Fhearchair keep word-lists side by side through the season of speech-making. Wren's list survives in the Administration's letter-books. Gormshuil's is lost; only its first leaf, with forty words for the colours of broken coal, is known from a copy.
- **23 an Giblean, AE 3** — *One word for the coal* (Cathair dhearg). The humans have a single word for the coloured coal, and it is their word for the black fuel they burn at home. Gormshuil's copyist notes that no Dia-thìris word in either list answers to it, and that the humans did not ask for one.
- **24 an Cèitean, AE 3** — *Trade begins*. At first the trade is fair on both sides: the goods of Dia-thìr for tools and knowledge the lonely island lacks. For a few years it seems it may last.
- **22 an t-Ògmhios, AE 3** — *The trading post at Ros dhomhain* (Ros dhomhain). The humans set up a trading post at Ros dhomhain, the capital's harbour, and give iron tools, window glass, lamp-oil and paper for wool, salt fish, hides and dyed cloth. The first tally-book of the post, kept by the trader Thomas Pike, balances evenly through its first year.
- **21 an t-Iuchar, AE 3** — *The first hull on Loch chrom* (Abhainn gheal). Pilots of Caol leathan bring the first of the strangers' ships up the Abhainn gheal into Loch chrom, towing her with boats through the shallows below Baile ghlas, and she anchors off Ros dhomhain. Thereafter the humans' goods come to the capital shore by water, and the pilots charge a stranger's hull twice the toll of a Dia-thìrich boat.
- **19 an Lùnastal, AE 3** — *Cathair naomh sends its wool* (Cathair naomh). Cathair naomh, the city above Seann Toll on the northern coast, sends its first wool south to the humans' post by coasting boat. Its custodians take their payment in paper and ink, and with them begin the town's roll afresh.
- **17 an t-Sultain, AE 3** — *Iron in the smithies* (Cathair dhearg). The smiths of Cathair dhearg take the humans' bar-iron gladly and learn to temper it in a winter. Within a few seasons the old bronze hoes are melted down for bells.
- **4 an Dàmhair, AE 4** — *Dyes for Baile Mòr mhòr* (Baile Mòr mhòr). The weavers of Baile Mòr mhòr on the northern coast trade their cloth for the humans' dyes, a red and a blue brighter than any the island could make. Within a few years the old madder fields about the town go back to grass.
- **16 an Dàmhair, AE 4** — *Harrow's second voyage* (Cuan shean). Harrow sails west with hides and dyed cloth and comes back with four ships in place of three. He brings carpenters, a surgeon, and a letter from a trading house in an Tìr Thall asking what else the island has.
- **14 an t-Samhain, AE 4** — *The shipwrights of Inis mhòr* (Inis mhòr). The shipwrights of Inis mhòr come to look at the humans' hulls and measure them with knotted cords. Their guild had built nothing greater than a coaster since the fleet of the Sundering, and the old craft of building for deep water was half forgotten.
- **13 an Dùbhlachd, AE 4** — *The surgeon Jonas Tull* (Cuan shean). The humans' surgeon, Jonas Tull, sets the broken leg of a fisherman of Cuan shean who had been given up as lame. The town's custodian enters it in the roll as the first debt owed to a stranger.
- **30 am Màrt, AE 5** — *Salt from Seann Warr* (Seann Warr). The salt-pans of Seann Warr begin to sell to Pike's post by the barrel. It is the first goods of Dia-thìr that the humans come back asking for twice.
- **14 an Giblean, AE 5** — *Wool at Caol leathan* (Caol leathan). The walled harbour of Caol leathan sends its first wool-ship to the humans' post. Its merchants will be paid only in iron by weight, and the tally-book of the post names them the hardest bargainers on the island.
- **22 an Giblean, AE 5** — *The first mixed settlement*. A small coastal town takes in both Dia-thìrich and humans under one rule. It is not tried again.
- **10 an Dàmhair, AE 5** — *Baile dhìreach under one council* (Baile dhìreach). The small port of Baile dhìreach on the south-west coast takes Dia-thìrich and humans under one council of six, three of each. Its founding compact is written twice, once in each tongue, the only such compact of the age.
- **18 an Dàmhair, AE 5** — *The first council of Baile dhìreach* (Baile dhìreach). The council is chaired in alternate years by the fisherman Iain mac Chaluim and the human carpenter William Rook. The harbour dues go half to the custodians at Cathair dhearg and half to the humans' post.
- **1 am Faoilleach, AE 6** — *Inis thais declines the compact* (Inis thais). The city of Inis thais, whose harbour lies a few miles from Baile dhìreach, is bidden to join the joint council and declines. Its custodian writes that one town may be a trial, but two would be a rule.
- **30 am Faoilleach, AE 6** — *A supply ship lost on the western reefs* (Muir Mhanannain). A human supply ship strikes the reefs off the western coast in fog, and nine of her crew drown. Her master was sailing by a chart drawn from memory, the humans' letter-books complain, on a coast lit only by the old driftwood fires.
- **28 an Gearran, AE 6** — *The beacons asked for*. Human seamen, strange to the coasts of Dia-thìr, ask for standing beacons. The builders of the Dia-thìrich agree, not yet seeing what the beacons will bring.
- **29 am Màrt, AE 6** — *The beacon headlands walked* (Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg). The human navigator James Fenn and the Dia-thìrich mason Torcall Clachair walk the coast together to choose the places of the new beacons, and mark the five headlands of the old fires. Fenn's chart survives; Torcall's cairns for the most part do not.
- **26 an Giblean, AE 7** — *Fenn's line* (Dia-thìr). On the same survey James Fenn runs a line of sights across the whole island, from the open sea off the north-west, where ships from the west first raise the land, to the water off the eastern cape. He makes it two hundred and twenty-one miles, some forty-five of them sea at the western end. It is the first measure of Dia-thìr from side to side, and every chart the Company draws afterwards is scaled to it.
- **26 an Cèitean, AE 7** — *A marriage in two tongues* (Baile dhìreach). At Baile dhìreach the net-maker Eilidh nic Ruairidh weds the human cooper Samuel Hale. The council enters the marriage in both its books; the custodians at Cathair dhearg, asked for a ruling, send none.
- **27 an Giblean, AE 8** — *The first written treaty*. The terms on which the humans stay are first set down in writing, in the humans' tongue only. No one among the Dia-thìrich speaks against it at the time.
- **7 an Cèitean, AE 8** — *The treaty signed at Cathair dhearg* (Cathair dhearg). The treaty is signed in the council hall at Cathair dhearg by Tormod mac Ailein for the custodians, and for the Administration by Josiah Pell, newly come as the humans' first Commissioner. Tormod could not read the tongue it was written in. Who read it to him is not told.
- **10 an Cèitean, AE 9** — *The Residency above Ros dhomhain* (Ros dhomhain). Josiah Pell builds a house of dressed stone on the rise above Ros dhomhain and calls it the Residency. Captain Harrow, needed ashore no longer, goes back to the sea trade.
- **18 an Cèitean, AE 9** — *The Company chartered* (Ros dhomhain). Harrow and Pike found a trading house under licence of the Administration, known on Dia-thìr simply as the Company. Its charter gives it first refusal of "all fuels, ores and minerals the island may yield."
- **28 an Dàmhair, AE 9** — *The warehouse at Cathair dhomhain* (Cathair dhomhain). The Company leases a stone warehouse at Cathair dhomhain, along the lake shore from the capital, to keep its tools from the harbour thieves of Ros dhomhain. It is the first building on Dia-thìr the Company owns outright.
- **5 an t-Samhain, AE 9** — *The strangers' fever* (Cuan shean). A fever comes ashore at Cuan shean with a crowded ship and runs down the west coast. Ninety-one Dia-thìrich die, and eleven humans. The custodians shut the town to ships for a season, and Pell protests in writing.
- **9 an Gearran, AE 10** — *The fever at Baile àrsaidh* (Baile àrsaidh). The strangers' fever comes to Baile àrsaidh, a day's walk up the coast, and kills its custodian and both her sons. No humans dwell in the town at all, and the custodians of the west take note of it.
- **14 an t-Samhain, AE 10** — *The fever turned back at Cnoc àrsaidh* (Cnoc àrsaidh). At Cnoc àrsaidh in the south-west the townsfolk block the road with carts and turn back every traveller for a season, and the fever does not reach them. The Administration fines the town for hindering trade.
- **13 an Dùbhlachd, AE 10** — *Prospectors in the central hills* (Muileann chrom). The Company sends two prospectors, Abel Stone and Hugh Mercer, into the hills east of the capital. They come back with sacks of broken coal, and word that the black seam runs "further than can be walked in a day."
- **17 an t-Sultain, AE 11** — *The sacks returned to the rock* (Muileann chrom). The custodians of the vein demand the broken coal back, to lay it in the rock again with the proper words. The Company returns half. The custodians' roll enters the other half as "carried west."
- **19 an t-Sultain, AE 11** — *The first mining contracts*. Trade sours into bargain. Dia-thìrich hands mine the vein on a scale that no reverent custom had ever used.
- **16 an Dàmhair, AE 11** — *The first pit at Muileann chrom* (Muileann chrom). Under the first contract a Dia-thìrich crew of thirty opens a working at Muileann chrom, paid by the ton in iron tools and lamp-oil. The custodians' own cuttings had never been measured by weight at all.
- **23 an t-Iuchar, AE 12** — *A coal quay at Ceann fhada* (Ceann fhada). The Company builds a stone quay at Ceann fhada, a fishing hamlet below the hills, for loading coal into coasting barges. The fishermen are paid for their foreshore in iron nails, by weight.
- **21 an Lùnastal, AE 12** — *Wren's grammar* (Ros dhomhain). Samuel Wren finishes a grammar of Dia-thìris for the Mission, the house of the humans' Church on Dia-thìr. It is careful and true in most things, and it gives the word for the vein's custodians as "keepers of the coal."
- **4 an t-Iuchar, AE 13** — *The hawk-priests read Wren* (Cnoc bheag). The hawk-priests of Cnoc bheag ask the Mission for a copy of Wren's grammar, to read what the humans write of them. The Mission sends one. Of all the copies that survive it bears the most notes in the margins.
- **30 an Dùbhlachd, AE 13** — *The Mission chapel* (Ros dhomhain). The Mission raises a timber chapel on the quay at Ros dhomhain, the first church on the island. Its bell is the first iron bell on the island, and the custodians ask that it not be rung before the fishing fleet is out.
- **29 am Màrt, AE 14** — *The first refusal*. One mining settlement will not sign a contract. For the present it is passed by, not punished.
- **27 an Giblean, AE 14** — *Beathag Dhubh of Doire mhòr* (Doire mhòr). The settlement that refused was Doire mhòr, in the hills above Muileann chrom, and its custodian was Beathag Dhubh. Her answer to the Company's agent is known only in his words: that the hill was not hers to sell nor his to buy.
- **28 an Gearran, AE 15** — *The road around Doire mhòr* (Cnoc fhiadhaich). The Company opens its next working at Cnoc fhiadhaich instead, and runs its cart-road round the fields of Doire mhòr and not through them.
- **9 an Cèitean, AE 15** — *Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg lit* (Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg). The first of the new beacons is finished on the southern headland at Tobar dhearg: a round tower of grey stone raised over the old fire-tower, paid for by the Company, with a Dia-thìrich keeper. Torcall Clachair builds it; James Fenn sets its lens.
- **29 am Màrt, AE 16** — *The first keeper of Tobar dhearg* (Tobar dhearg). The first keeper of the southern beacon is Anna nic Dhòmhnaill of Tobar dhearg village, a fisherman's widow, who climbs the tower twice a night for the rest of her life. The village holds the keepership as a trust and keeps it in its own families through the age.
- **10 an Giblean, AE 16** — *Raiders in the north-western waters* (Spùinneadairean-mara). A Company brig is boarded off the north-west coast and stripped of her cargo of tools. The raiders are never known. The Administration blames the custodians of the coast, and the custodians answer that those waters have always kept their own law.
- **5 an Gearran, AE 17** — *The obelisk at Cnoc bheag copied* (Carragh Cnoc bheag). Samuel Wren copies the writing on the obelisk near Cnoc bheag and sends it west to the scholars of an Tìr Thall. No answer comes. The custodians tell him the stone is older than the Dia-thìrich and that none living can read it.
- **13 an Gearran, AE 17** — *The first coin*. The humans' coin is brought in beside the old barter, for ease, it is said. Within ten years nothing that needs a tool from over the sea can be had for anything else.
- **10 an Lùnastal, AE 17** — *The mark and its hundred pence* (Ros dhomhain). The coins are struck at Ros dhomhain from silver and copper shipped from an Tìr Thall: the mark and its hundred pence. The first striking bears a ship on one face, and nothing of Dia-thìr on either.
- **1 am Faoilleach, AE 18** — *Cathair mhòr refuses the mark* (Cathair mhòr). The market of Cathair mhòr, greatest below the hills east of the capital, refuses the humans' coin for a whole year. The custodians of the town give way when the Company's tool-sellers will not cross their bridge.
- **30 am Faoilleach, AE 18** — *Two books at the capital market* (Cathair dhearg). At the market of Cathair dhearg the tool-sellers take only marks, while cloth and fish still go by barter. The custodians' clerks begin to keep two sets of books, and complain of it in both.
- **3 an Dùbhlachd, AE 18** — *Wren's winter at Dùn thais* (Dùn thais). The masters of the druid school at Dùn thais receive Samuel Wren for a winter of disputation. He asks them why the vein should be holy; they ask him why his fuel should be burned. Neither telling of that winter names a winner.
- **28 an Gearran, AE 19** — *Drochaid Cathair dhearg rebuilt* (Drochaid Cathair dhearg). Company masons rebuild in dressed stone the old bridge over Abhainn dhomhain at Cathair dhearg, wide enough for coal-carts to pass two abreast.
- **30 an t-Sultain, AE 19** — *The Commissioner's carriage* (Drochaid Cathair dhearg). Company wheelwrights build a closed carriage for Josiah Pell, and he drives in it over the new bridge from the Residency to the council at Cathair dhearg. It is the first carriage on the island. The custodians still walk to the council, and say so.
- **16 an t-Samhain, AE 19** — *The Harbour Articles* (Ros dhomhain). A second compact, the Harbour Articles, fixes the dues and anchorages of Ros dhomhain in the Company's favour. Like the first treaty it is written in the humans' tongue only, and this time two custodians refuse to sign.
- **5 an Dàmhair, AE 20** — *The fishermen of Baile ghlas* (Baile ghlas). The fishermen of Baile ghlas, whose boats had anchored free at Ros dhomhain time out of mind, are charged anchorage under the Harbour Articles. They take their catch to their own small harbour and sell it there to anyone but the Company.
- **3 an t-Samhain, AE 20** — *The northern concession* (Muileann àrsaidh). The council grants the Administration upland pasture in the north-west about Muileann àrsaidh, for human families who will not work in the pits. The grant is for grazing; the families build houses of stone.
- **15 an Dùbhlachd, AE 20** — *Death of Tormod mac Ailein* (Cathair dhearg). Tormod mac Ailein, the high custodian who signed the first treaty, dies at Cathair dhearg. The council chooses Coinneach Glas of Ceann àrsaidh after him, who had never met a human before the Crossing and has dealt with little else since.
- **10 an t-Iuchar, AE 21** — *Harrow lost at sea* (Muir Mhanannain). Edmund Harrow's ship does not come back from the western crossing. The Company passes wholly into Thomas Pike's hands, and the humans' letter-books mourn Harrow as the man who found Dia-thìr.
- **2 an Dùbhlachd, AE 21** — *The Small-Burning Law lapses*. Centuries of measured burning end within one generation. The Law is never repealed; once its keeping no longer pays, it is no longer kept.
- **31 an Dùbhlachd, AE 21** — *The last count at Doire mhin* (Doire mhin). The custodians of Doire mhin keep the old count of the Small-Burning Law, the measure of coal that might be burned in a year, one season longer than any others. They enter it in their roll with the note that no one asked for it.
- **11 an t-Ògmhios, AE 22** — *A defence of the Law at Dùn dhearg* (Dùn dhearg). Fionnghal nic Artair, a custodian of Dùn dhearg, writes to the council in defence of the Small-Burning Law, the only such defence that survives. She holds that the Law was never for the coal's sake but for the people, who would become whatever the burning made them.
- **6 an t-Sultain, AE 22** — *Murchadh Seabhag preaches at Seann Skell* (Seann Skell). At Seann Skell the hawk-priest Murchadh Seabhag preaches that Mòd, the Hungry Hawk of Acaill, starves those who eat faster than the land can feed them. The sermon is copied and carried to the camps, and it is the first writing of the Dia-thìrich that the Company's agents are told to seize.
- **16 am Màrt, AE 23** — *The hearths of Achadh naomh* (Achadh naomh). The households of Achadh naomh, in the hills north of the workings, who keep Na Seann Spioradan, will not light their hearths with coal bought of the Company. They burn peat as their grandparents did, and their elders teach that coal burned for wages is burned without the ancestors' leave.
- **8 an Lùnastal, AE 23** — *Burning by the cartload* (Muileann chrom). The Company's furnaces at Muileann chrom burn coal by the cartload to drive the new pumps, and no heed is paid to the custodians' tally of what the hill may give in a year. Coinneach Glas's council asks that the tally be kept, and is sent a copy of the Company's accounts.
- **15 an Gearran, AE 24** — *Henry Maddox Commissioner* (Ros dhomhain). Josiah Pell sails home to an Tìr Thall and does not return. After him comes Henry Maddox, bidden to double the yield, with a letter from the Company promising him a share of it.
- **12 am Màrt, AE 24** — *The oaks of Cathair fhada* (Cathair fhada). Maddox buys the oak woods about Cathair fhada for pit-props. The town had cut them sparingly for generations; they are gone within the working lives of the men who fell them.
- **26 an Giblean, AE 25** — *The first deaths of haste*. A tunnel worked faster than any Dia-thìrich crew would have worked it falls in and kills eleven. It is entered as an accident.
- **14 an Dàmhair, AE 25** — *The eleven of Cnoc fhiadhaich* (Cnoc fhiadhaich). The fall was at Cnoc fhiadhaich, in a gallery driven forward without the timbering the Dia-thìrich crews had asked for. The custodians' roll names all eleven dead. The Company's report names none, and calls the gallery "unsound ground."
- **11 an Gearran, AE 26** — *The coughing sickness* (Muileann chrom). A dry cough runs through the camps at Muileann chrom and Cnoc fhiadhaich, worst among the boys who break coal at the pit-mouth, and thirty-eight die of it. The Mission's surgeon calls it a winter complaint. It lasts through the summer.
- **6 an t-Iuchar, AE 27** — *The orphans of Cill thais* (Cill thais). The village of Cill thais takes in the children orphaned by the coughing sickness and keeps a house for them at its own custodians' cost. The Company, asked to give toward it, sends a crate of Mission primers.
- **4 an Lùnastal, AE 27** — *Taigh-solais Baile ìseal lit* (Taigh-solais Baile ìseal). The second beacon is lit on the eastern shore at Baile ìseal. Torcall Clachair, now too old to climb, directs its building from a chair at the foot of the headland.
- **9 an Cèitean, AE 28** — *The keepers of Baile ìseal* (Baile ìseal). The keepers of the eastern beacon are drawn from the fishing families of Baile ìseal. The town's custodians ask for a rule, and get it, that the lamp be lowered on the nights the boats go out to the deep grounds, lest the fish take fright. When the rule lapsed no one wrote down.
- **23 an Giblean, AE 29** — *Seòlaid Ceann òg* (Ceann òg). The traders' boats from the new quay at Ceann òg go down the Abhainn ìseal past Cnoc bheag and Inis bhàn to the north coast, west along it, round the western capes, and south past Inis thais into the capital's water. Their lane is called Seòlaid Ceann òg after the quay. Off the north-west it swings far out into the open sea, and there the ships bound for an Tìr Thall leave it and the ships from the west come in.
- **6 an Dàmhair, AE 29** — *The camp at Àth ìseal* (Àth ìseal). The Company builds a camp of timber huts at Àth ìseal, at the ford below the new workings, for crews brought in from the coast. It is the first settlement on Dia-thìr made for nothing but the pit.
- **23 an t-Iuchar, AE 30** — *Doire mhòr's water taken* (Doire mhòr). The Company turns the stream that watered Doire mhòr to wash coal at Cnoc fhiadhaich. No order is written; the stream is dammed one season and not let go. Beathag Dhubh's people carry water by hand for two summers, and then begin to leave.
- **21 an Lùnastal, AE 30** — *The short hunger in the hills* (Muileann chrom). The men drawn from the farms into the pits, the hill villages of Muileann chrom lose their oats to rain, with none at home to cut ahead of it. The Company sells meal at the camp stores for marks, and the villages have few.
- **15 an Dàmhair, AE 31** — *Meal-carts at Doire fhiadhaich* (Doire fhiadhaich). The villages of Doire fhiadhaich in the south send carts of meal north to the hill villages, as the old custom of the Holy Age bids in a hungry year. The Company's agents at Àth ìseal buy up two of the carts on the road.
- **13 an t-Samhain, AE 31** — *The mountain dug by the ton*. For the first time in the history of Dia-thìr the mountain is worked by the ton, and for ends no custom of the Dia-thìrich would have chosen.
- **12 an Dùbhlachd, AE 31** — *Rope for the winding-gear* (Dùn chrom). The rope-walks of Dùn chrom, which had made cable for the fishing boats, turn wholly to winding-rope for the pit-heads. The Company pays well, and the town grows by half.
- **7 an Giblean, AE 32** — *The Company's second charter* (Ros dhomhain). The Company is chartered again in an Tìr Thall, with new money and a new name the Dia-thìrich never take up. Its agents at Ros dhomhain now outnumber the Administration's own clerks four to one.
- **16 an t-Sultain, AE 32** — *Barges at Cidhe Beag* (Cidhe Beag). Coal barges begin to load at Cidhe Beag on Abhainn uaine and float the black coal down to the coast. The old canoe landing, used since before the Sundering, is widened with cut stone, and its shrine is moved uphill.
- **27 am Faoilleach, AE 33** — *Abhainn uaine silts black* (Abhainn uaine). The washing of coal upstream fills Abhainn uaine with black slurry, and within a few seasons the salmon runs at its mouth fail. The river keeps its name, the green river, and the fishermen speak it bitterly.
- **1 an Lùnastal, AE 33** — *Baile Mòr dhomhain a barge town* (Baile Mòr dhomhain). As the coal comes down to it from Cidhe Beag, Baile Mòr dhomhain on the river road grows into the busiest barge town of the north. Its people double in number, most of the newcomers bargemen from the coast.
- **10 am Faoilleach, AE 34** — *Baile dhomhain raised as a camp town* (Baile dhomhain). A Company surveyor lays out a second camp, Baile dhomhain, on a grid, the first town of the Dia-thìrich drawn on paper before it was built. Within two seasons it houses four hundred.
- **1 an Lùnastal, AE 34** — *An Taigh-seinnse Mòr reopens* (An Taigh-seinnse Mòr). The old carters' house at the half-way stage of the coal road between the capital and the hills is built again, opens its doors at Lùnastal, and keeps the name An Taigh-seinnse Mòr. Its first keeper, Seònaid Bhàn, takes both marks and barter, the only innkeeper on the road who will.
- **17 an t-Sultain, AE 34** — *Rathad na Mèinne* (Àth chiar). The Company's road-gangs finish metalling the carriers' road from Cathair dhearg by Doire chaol and the ford of Àth chiar to the workings at Achadh dhomhain, wide enough for coal-carts to pass both ways. The carters call it Rathad na Mèinne, the mine road. The posts with the crown's sign that had marked it since the Age of Sundering are left standing along it.
- **20 an Giblean, AE 35** — *The carters of Doire chaol* (Doire chaol). The carters of Doire chaol, on the road just east of the capital, band together in a guild to bargain with the Company over the rates for hauling coal. It is the first Dia-thìrich guild of the age, and the Company owns it because that is cheaper than breaking it.
- **3 an t-Iuchar, AE 35** — *Seann Toll made a coal landing* (Seann Toll). The Company takes the river landing at Seann Toll, below the workings, and builds a loading stage there for the barges that carry the coal down the Abhainn uaine to Ceann leathan. The town's fishing boats are moved to the next reach.
- **31 am Faoilleach, AE 36** — *The coal ships' lane* (Ceann leathan). From the landing at Seann Toll the coal barges go down the Abhainn uaine to Ceann leathan, where the Company's ships load at the river mouth and go out by the southern lane, Slighe-mhara Caol fhiadhaich, west along the south coast to the wild strait and the open sea. The fishers of the south coast, who had used the lane for five hundred years, learn to keep out of the coal ships' way.
- **19 an Cèitean, AE 36** — *The first Dia-thìrich overseer*. A Dia-thìrich is set over other Dia-thìrich miners, answerable to human masters. It is the first open crack within the Dia-thìrich themselves, and not only between them and the humans.
- **17 an t-Ògmhios, AE 36** — *Raghnall Maor* (Muileann chrom). The first overseer is Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill of Muileann chrom, a crew-leader who had worked the pits since the first contract. He is given the Company's staff and a house with a slate roof, and from the office the Dia-thìrich give him his byname: Raghnall Maor, Raghnall the steward.
- **21 an Lùnastal, AE 37** — *The overseers multiply* (Muileann chrom). Within a few years there are overseers at every working in the district, all Dia-thìrich, all answerable to the Company's agents. The custodians' roll no longer names them, and gives only their number.
- **14 an Lùnastal, AE 38** — *Seumas Dubh killed at Cnoc mhòr* (Cnoc mhòr). Seumas Dubh, overseer of the new pits at Cnoc mhòr, is killed by his own crew after a boy is crushed on a haulage he had ordered hurried. The Company hangs two men at Ros dhomhain, the first hanging done by the Administration on Dia-thìr.
- **12 an t-Sultain, AE 38** — *Hawk-priests barred from the camps* (Muileann chrom). Henry Maddox bars the priests of Òrd an t-Seabhaig from the camps, for their preaching slows the work. The overseers enforce the order, though several of them are hawk-faithful, as the roll says. The Mission's chaplains, who keep a chapel in every camp, are not barred.
- **11 an Dàmhair, AE 39** — *The pox at Ros dhomhain* (Ros dhomhain). A spotted pox comes ashore at Ros dhomhain on a Company ship and climbs the coal road into the camps. The Mission counts four hundred and six dead. The custodians count more, and write the difference in the margin of the Mission's list.
- **9 an t-Samhain, AE 40** — *The pox in the south* (Baile chiar). The pox spreads south from the harbour to Baile chiar and the villages about it. The custodians there cut the names of the dead into the stone lintel of the council house, and they can still be read.
- **31 am Faoilleach, AE 41** — *Baile dhìreach loses its harbour dues* (Baile dhìreach). The Administration moves its customs house from Baile dhìreach to Ros dhomhain and ends the sharing of the harbour dues. The mixed council, left with half an income, cuts its members from six to four.
- **28 an t-Iuchar, AE 41** — *Arthur Lisle Commissioner* (Ros dhomhain). Henry Maddox leaves Dia-thìr a rich man. Arthur Lisle, a lawyer, comes after him, and his first act is to have every compact since the first treaty copied into one bound book.
- **2 am Màrt, AE 42** — *A customs house at Ros gheal* (Ros gheal). Lisle opens a second customs house at Ros gheal on the northern coast, where hawk-faithful fishing towns had traded with Company ships without paying dues. The customs officer is twice chased out of the town in his first year.
- **3 am Faoilleach, AE 43** — *The silver of Muileann chiar* (Muileann chiar — baile mèinne airgid). The humans seek to claim the silver seam at Muileann chiar as well. It is one of the few things the Dia-thìrich keep wholly in their own hands through all this age.
- **31 am Màrt, AE 43** — *Ùna nic Choinnich and the silver guild* (Muileann chiar — baile mèinne airgid). The silver seam was held for the town by its guild of refiners, led by Ùna nic Choinnich. When the Company's surveyors came she met them at the adit with every member of the guild and all its ledgers, and bade them find the humans' name anywhere in either.
- **1 an Gearran, AE 44** — *The Silver Compact* (Muileann chiar — baile mèinne airgid). Arthur Lisle, reading the treaties closely, finds nothing in them touching silver. On Là Fhèill Brìde he signs a compact with the silver guild leaving the seam to the town, the first writing of the age in which the Dia-thìrich keep the better terms.
- **26 an t-Ògmhios, AE 44** — *Seann Bhral the silver port* (Seann Bhral). The silver guild sends its bars to the sea by the old port of Seann Bhral and not by the Company's quays, and pays the port's custodians in silver for the use of it. The Company finds no ground in the compact to object.
- **21 am Faoilleach, AE 45** — *The carters of Baile gheal* (Baile gheal). The carters of Baile gheal in the south-west take up the carrying of Seann Warr brine-salt round the lake to the capital, a trade the Company does not trouble to claim. It keeps the town's folk out of the pits for the whole age.
- **10 an t-Iuchar, AE 45** — *Taigh-solais Àth dhearg lit* (Taigh-solais Àth dhearg). The third beacon is lit on the north-east coast at Àth dhearg. Its keeper, Tormod mac Pheadair, keeps a daybook of every ship he sees, and from his book the number of human sailings in these years is known.
- **28 an Cèitean, AE 46** — *Àth dhearg builds the tower* (Àth dhearg). The masons of the beacon at Àth dhearg are its own townsmen, paid half in marks and half in the promise that the tower will guide their own boats home. Tormod mac Pheadair, the keeper, is one of them.
- **20 an Dàmhair, AE 46** — *Pirates off the eastern coast* (Spùinneadairean-mara). Raiders in low black boats take a Company coal ship off the eastern coast and burn her to the waterline, cargo and all. The Company says the silver guild paid them. The silver guild says nothing.
- **25 an t-Iuchar, AE 47** — *A cove burned near Ceann leathan* (Ceann leathan). A Company gunboat hunts the raiders to a cove near Ceann leathan and burns every boat drawn up on the shingle, most of them belonging to the town's fishermen. The raiders are not found.
- **23 an Lùnastal, AE 47** — *The end of the joint council* (Baile dhìreach). The mixed council of Baile dhìreach breaks up in a quarrel over a boundary wall and never meets again. The human families go to Ros bheag and Ros dhomhain; the Dia-thìrich families stay. Households that were both split or fell silent, and which did which is not told.
- **18 an t-Samhain, AE 47** — *The boatyard moves to Inis chrom* (Inis chrom). The human boatbuilders of Baile dhìreach move their yard to Inis chrom, a day's sail east, where the Company has promised them timber. The town takes them in without a joint council or any other compact, and within a generation they fade from its rolls.
- **21 an t-Sultain, AE 48** — *The dry year in the east* (Achadh shean). For a single season the rain fails over the eastern farmlands about Achadh shean. It is remembered after as a warning no one heeded, for the next drought, long after, came three years together.
- **20 an Dàmhair, AE 48** — *Baile ruadh loses its seed* (Baile ruadh). At Baile ruadh in the east the drought kills the seed corn in the ground, and the town borrows seed from the Company's store at Seann Dunn, at a price paid back over five harvests. It is the first Dia-thìrich town to owe the Company a debt in grain.
- **19 an t-Ògmhios, AE 49** — *Aonghas mac Coinnich's question* (Dùn thais). At Dùn thais the druid master Aonghas mac Coinnich puts to his students a question the school's register calls new: why the humans cannot see the colour in broken coal that every Dia-thìrich child sees. He does not answer it, and the register notes that he called it the wrong question.
- **15 an Dùbhlachd, AE 49** — *The druid students of Baile Mòr uaine* (Baile Mòr uaine). Students of Aonghas mac Coinnich carry his question to Baile Mòr uaine and teach it in the town's hall of disputation. The hall's record of the argument runs to four hundred leaves, and ends, like his, without an answer.
- **28 an Cèitean, AE 50** — *Cathair gheal in the northern concession* (Cathair gheal). The human families of the northern concession found a market town at Cathair gheal, with a stone hall for their magistrate and a chapel. The Administration issues its charter without asking the custodians.
- **26 an t-Ògmhios, AE 50** — *Human farms at Cnoc ghorm* (Cnoc ghorm). Human farmers of the concession clear land beside the Dia-thìrich village of Cnoc ghorm in the upland north-west, and build a mill. The villagers sell them grain until the mill is working, and then stop.
- **14 am Màrt, AE 51** — *A fishing station at Ceann mhòr* (Ceann mhòr). A few human fishing families of the concession settle at Ceann mhòr, the harbour under the north-western headland. They are the first humans to fish the island's waters for a living and not for the Company's table.
- **10 an Giblean, AE 51** — *The first Dia-thìrich child sent over the sea*. One family, hoping for better treatment, sends a son to be schooled in the humans' homeland. He is never known to return.
- **12 an Giblean, AE 51** — *The family of Eachann Mòr* (Ceann àrsaidh). The family that sent its son away was that of Eachann Mòr, a custodian of Ceann àrsaidh who had lost his seat on the council. The boy, Calum, sailed west on a Company ship with a letter from the Mission and a purse of marks.
- **9 an Cèitean, AE 51** — *The Mission school* (Ros dhomhain). The Mission opens a school at Ros dhomhain for Dia-thìrich children, taught in the humans' tongue. It takes thirty pupils in its first year, most of them overseers' children, and among them the Mission counts its first Dia-thìrich converts.
- **7 an t-Ògmhios, AE 52** — *Schooling at Inis bhàn* (Inis bhàn). The custodians of Inis bhàn in the north open a school of their own in answer to the Mission's, and teach the old reckoning, the rolls and the names of the hills. The Mission complains that the pupils come to its school the next year already knowing how to argue.
- **31 an Dàmhair, AE 52** — *Tobacco on the concession farms* (Ceann mhòr). Human farmers of the northern concession plant tobacco on the sheltered slopes behind Ceann mhòr and sell the dried leaf to the Company's ships. Of the crops the humans brought, it alone is still grown on Dia-thìr.
- **1 an Giblean, AE 53** — *Drochaid Ros fhionn* (Drochaid Ros fhionn). The Company rebuilds the old bridge over the river at Ros fhionn to carry the eastern coal road. While the carts run it is the busiest crossing on that side of the island.
- **29 an Dàmhair, AE 53** — *Coal through Inis bheag* (Inis bheag). Coal from the eastern workings is carted over the new bridge and down to the river quays of Inis bheag, and goes by barge to Caol chrom at the river mouth for shipping. The Company deepens the river at the quays, and the town's old fish market is moved to make room for the coal stage.
- **13 am Faoilleach, AE 54** — *Baile mhin ships the eastern coal* (Baile mhin). The river quays of Baile mhin, below Inis bheag on the Abhainn bheag, take the eastern coal that Inis bheag cannot load. The townsfolk are paid by the barge, and with the gain the town builds its first stone houses.
- **11 an Gearran, AE 54** — *Caol gharbh passed by* (Caol gharbh). The coal road to Inis bheag passes Caol gharbh by a mile, and the town, which had hoped for the traffic, gets only its dust. Its custodians write that they had not known a town could be harmed by a road it was not on.
- **12 am Màrt, AE 55** — *The thing in the north-western sea* (Uilebheist na Mara). The crew of a Company brig see a beast greater than their ship off the north-western headlands. The Administration's clerk files their report with the complaints about pirates, and the Dia-thìrich sailors of the coast say they had wondered when the humans would see it.
- **13 an t-Sultain, AE 55** — *A brig lost in the mist* (Caol bheag). A Company brig bound for the northern landing with tools is caught by a gale in sea mist off Eilean fhada and driven onto the skerries. Her crew wade ashore at low water and walk to the harbour at Caol bheag. Thereafter the Company's charts mark the northern passage closed to its ships from midwinter to the end of spring, the season of the gales.
- **9 an Dùbhlachd, AE 55** — *Whale-boats out of Àth fhionn* (Àth fhionn). Human fishermen of the concession teach the boats of Àth fhionn to hunt whales with the hand-lance, and not wait for them to strand. The oil is sold to the Company for its lamps, and from this time whale-boats go out from the north coast every summer.
- **21 an Lùnastal, AE 56** — *Surveyors lost at Doire uaine* (Marbh-bheò Doire uaine). Two Company surveyors go up into the hills at Doire uaine against the villagers' counsel and are not seen again. The Company sends a search party, which comes back after a day and will go no further.
- **19 an t-Sultain, AE 56** — *The offerings at Doire uaine* (Doire uaine). After the surveyors are lost the villagers of Doire uaine leave salt and coal for the sìth at the foot of the hills, as their grandparents did after any death on the high ground. The Company forbids coal to be left lying and has the offerings gathered up, and the villagers leave salt alone.
- **16 an Gearran, AE 57** — *The tithe raised*. The share of mined coal taken by the humans' Administration rises steeply. What the Dia-thìrich receive does not rise with it.
- **13 an Lùnastal, AE 57** — *Lisle's tithe schedule* (Ros dhomhain). The new schedule goes out from the Residency under Arthur Lisle's hand and raises the Administration's share from one part in five to one part in three. The custodians receive a copy in the humans' tongue, with a rendering made by a Mission pupil.
- **4 an Lùnastal, AE 58** — *Weighing the grain at Dùn fhiadhaich* (Dùn fhiadhaich). At Dùn fhiadhaich the tithe-gatherers begin to weigh grain as well as coal, saying the town's farms feed the pits and share in their gain. The custodians' roll calls it the tithe on the tithe.
- **6 an t-Iuchar, AE 59** — *The flux at Ros dhomhain* (Ros dhomhain). A bloody flux breaks out in the crowded quarters at the Ros dhomhain quays. The Mission's nurse, Anne Colby, makes a sick-house of the chapel, and it is said that she kept the dead below two hundred.
- **7 an t-Ògmhios, AE 60** — *The flux reaches Seann Vell* (Seann Vell). The coal barges carry the flux to Seann Vell, the river port east of the capital on the Abhainn fhionn. The custodians of the town shut the barge landing for a season, and the Company fines them for it.
- **3 am Màrt, AE 61** — *Walter Crane Commissioner* (Ros dhomhain). Arthur Lisle dies at the Residency of a fever of the heart. Walter Crane, who had been the Company's chief agent at the pits, is made Commissioner after him, the first to hold both offices one after the other.
- **6 an t-Sultain, AE 61** — *The pay office at Ceann mhin* (Ceann mhin). Crane moves the Company's pay office for the southern workings to Ceann mhin, and makes the crews walk there to be paid, a day each way, in place of sending the paymaster to them. The crews are not paid for the walk.
- **12 am Màrt, AE 62** — *Dòmhnall mac Raghnaill Maor* (Muileann chrom). Raghnall Maor dies, and the Company gives his staff to his son Dòmhnall. The overseer's office, which the custodians had hoped would die with the man, becomes a family's inheritance.
- **11 an Gearran, AE 63** — *Taigh-solais Muileann bheag lit* (Taigh-solais Muileann bheag). The fourth beacon is lit on the northern shore at Muileann bheag, the first to burn coal and not oil. Its keepers say the flame throws a colour on the water that no oil lamp ever did.
- **13 am Faoilleach, AE 64** — *The fishermen of Muileann bheag* (Muileann bheag). The fishermen of Muileann bheag complain that the colour the coal flame casts on the water drives the herring off. The keepers do not change the lamp. Within a season the herring come back, and the complaint is withdrawn in a letter the Company keeps.
- **27 an Giblean, AE 64** — *The dig at Làrach an Teampaill* (Làrach an Teampaill). The Mission cleric Edwin Lowe digs for a season at Làrach an Teampaill with Company labourers, seeking proof of an older faith on the island. He finds cut stone, burnt bone and marks he cannot read, and writes that the ruin's builders "were not the present race." The custodians agree, and add nothing.
- **9 an Lùnastal, AE 65** — *The pillar at Cnoc chiar* (Colbh Cnoc chiar). Edwin Lowe copies the writing on the pillar near Cnoc chiar and sets it beside Wren's copy of the obelisk at Cnoc bheag. He judges that the two scripts are not the same, and that neither is of the Dia-thìrich. His notes stop there.
- **28 an Gearran, AE 66** — *The column at Cnoc ghorm* (Calbh Cnoc ghorm). Lowe's last copy is of the column near Cnoc ghorm, and beside it he writes that its marks are like the pillar's, but not near enough to help. He leaves Dia-thìr the next year and takes his notebooks with him.
- **8 an Lùnastal, AE 66** — *The glass-house at Baile Mòr dhìreach* (Baile Mòr dhìreach). Peter Voss, a glazier left behind when his Company contract ended, builds a glass-house at Baile Mòr dhìreach and melts the white sand of Cuan ruadh with charcoal from the hills. It is the first glass made on Dia-thìr. Within a generation his Dia-thìrich apprentices carry the craft to the towns of the capital shore.
- **29 am Màrt, AE 67** — *The silver guild refuses again* (Muileann chiar — baile mèinne airgid). Martha Gale, an agent of the Company, offers the silver guild of Muileann chiar a partnership, on terms the guild's ledger calls generous. Ùna nic Choinnich, now very old, has the offer read aloud twice in the guild hall, and it is refused by show of hands.
- **1 am Faoilleach, AE 68** — *The camp at Achadh dhomhain* (Achadh dhomhain). A new camp is opened at Achadh dhomhain for the deep galleries under the hill, and within a few seasons it is the most crowded place in the district. Its houses are built of spoil.
- **30 am Faoilleach, AE 68** — *Cloth for the camps at Dùn chiar* (Dùn chiar). The weavers of Dùn chiar take a Company contract for canvas for the camp tents and sacks for the coal, and the town thrives on it. Its custodians note that never before had the town made anything for a use it did not approve.
- **7 am Màrt, AE 69** — *The first of the undying generation*. A girl is born in the mining camps who takes more raw coal into her body over her life than any Dia-thìrich in living memory, and she does not age as the folk about her age. Her name is Aisling.
- **26 an t-Iuchar, AE 69** — *The coach to the camps* (Muileann chrom). The Company puts a coach on the road between the quay at Ros dhomhain and the camps at Muileann chrom, twice a week each way, changing horses at the old waypoint houses. Clerks and overseers ride in it. The crews walk.
- **3 an Dùbhlachd, AE 70** — *The coal weighed at the quay* (Ros dhomhain). The Company sets up a great steelyard at the Ros dhomhain quay, and thenceforth the island's yield is known by the ton and the hundredweight. The custodians' old count, kept in seasons of labour, is no longer entered in the roll.
- **15 an Dùbhlachd, AE 70** — *Ros dhìreach the second coal port* (Ros dhìreach). The Company opens a second coal stage at Ros dhìreach on the southern coast for the workings south of the hills. Its first cargo is lost in a squall off the harbour mouth, and the fishermen moved to make room for the stage will not go out after it.
- **13 am Faoilleach, AE 71** — *The nameless change*. What is befalling the child born two years before has as yet no name in any tongue spoken on the island. Decades pass before anyone tries to make one.
- **26 an Cèitean, AE 71** — *The first steamer* (Ros dhomhain). The first ship driven by an engine comes into Ros dhomhain, a Company paddle-steamer out of an Tìr Thall. The fishermen row out to look at a ship going against the wind with no sail set. Within a generation the Company's coal goes out in nothing else.
- **19 an t-Sultain, AE 72** — *The shrine at Cill dhìreach* (Cill dhìreach). At Cill dhìreach, a village at the edge of the workings, the custodians keep a small shrine where the pit crews leave the first piece of coal from each new gallery. The Company suffers the custom, for it costs a stone a gallery.
- **18 an Dàmhair, AE 72** — *The keepers of Cill ghlas* (Cill ghlas). The custodians of the shrine at Cill ghlas, in the hills among the workings, keep the old rites at the mouth of the oldest cutting while the Company's pits deepen about them. It is the last shrine in the district that the pit crews still visit on the old feast days.
- **9 an t-Ògmhios, AE 73** — *A' Phlàigh Uaine*. The Green Death goes through the mining camps. The coal dust is blamed, though no study of it is ever finished. Twenty-six settlements have cases.
- **5 an Dùbhlachd, AE 73** — *The first cases at Achadh dhomhain* (Achadh dhomhain). The Green Death is first marked at Achadh dhomhain: a greenish pallor, then a cough that brings up dark dust, then weakness. The camp buries forty in the first month, in a field beyond the spoil-heaps still called the green acre.
- **13 am Faoilleach, AE 74** — *Twenty-six settlements* (A' Phlàigh Uaine). The sickness spreads along the coal roads from the camps at Muileann chrom, Àth ìseal and Cnoc fhiadhaich, and falls hardest on Ros dhìreach, Ceann òg, Inis ìseal, Baile dhomhain, Achadh fhada, Cnoc bheag, Muileann uaine, Cuan àrsaidh and Inis bhàn. The custodians' roll lists the twenty-six settlements that had cases, and leaves a blank line after the last, as though waiting for another.
- **11 an Gearran, AE 74** — *The Green Death at Baile chrom* (Baile chrom). The Green Death comes to Baile chrom in the hills, not the town of that name in the north-west. The scribes keep the two apart with care, for in later tellings of the island's hungers they are confused.
- **12 am Màrt, AE 74** — *Àth ghlas burns its huts* (Àth ghlas). At Àth ghlas the custodians order every hut where a death has been burned with its bedding. The Company protests the loss of its property. The custodians note that the sickness stops sooner at Àth ghlas than anywhere else.
- **10 an Giblean, AE 74** — *The dead of Cnoc naomh* (Cnoc naomh). At Cnoc naomh the dead of the Green Death are laid in the burial ground of the town's old shrine until it is full, and then in a field outside. The field is never ploughed again.
- **30 am Faoilleach, AE 75** — *Doctor Bright's study* (Muileann chrom). Nathaniel Bright, physician to the Administration, begins to study the sickness at Muileann chrom, weighing the dust in the lungs of the dead. In the second season of the work he falls ill, and his notebooks break off in the middle of a table.
- **28 an Gearran, AE 75** — *Walter Crane dies of the Green Death* (Ros dhomhain). Commissioner Crane, who had walked the camps in the worst of the sickness, dies of it at the Residency. Martha Gale, the Company's agent at Ros dhomhain, holds his seal for the months until another comes.
- **13 am Màrt, AE 76** — *George Tolley Commissioner* (Ros dhomhain). George Tolley comes from an Tìr Thall with orders that the yield must not fall for the sickness. He does not visit the camps. His letter-book blames the dust, the Dia-thìrich custom of sleeping near the fire, and the custodians' shrines, in that order.
- **11 an Giblean, AE 76** — *Quarantine at Caol mhin* (Caol mhin). Tolley sets a quarantine station at Caol mhin on the northern coast for ships from an Tìr Thall, and holds them offshore until their crews are looked over. It is the first order of his rule the Dia-thìrich approve, and they say so.
- **10 an Cèitean, AE 76** — *The camps turn to the hawk* (Muileann chrom). The hawk-priests still barred from the camps, the crews carry their sermons in themselves. The overseers' reports of these years list hawk-feathers nailed above hut doors as a matter for punishment.
- **17 an Giblean, AE 77** — *Anne Colby's sick-houses* (Ros dhomhain). Anne Colby opens sick-houses at Àth ìseal and Achadh dhomhain and nurses there until the sickness ebbs. She is the only human the camp folk name in their own accounts of the plague, and they name her kindly.
- **25 an Giblean, AE 77** — *The huts of Cnoc gharbh* (Cnoc gharbh). After the sickness the people of Cnoc gharbh, who had worked the southern galleries, leave their camp huts and go back to the old village on the hill. The next year the Company builds the huts again and brings in crews from the west.
- **13 an Dàmhair, AE 77** — *The first strike*. A whole mining settlement stops work for eleven days over conditions worsened by the plague two years before. The strike ends when the food, which the humans' Administration holds, runs out.
- **21 an Dàmhair, AE 77** — *The strike at Baile thais* (Baile thais). The settlement was Baile thais, below Cill ghlas, and the crew-leader Catrìona nic Eachainn called the halt after the Company would not close the galleries where the Green Death had been worst. For eleven days no coal left the town. On the twelfth the Company's store, the only store, was empty.
- **2 an Dàmhair, AE 78** — *The Company's granary* (Baile thais). After the strike the Company builds a granary of its own at Muileann chrom and forbids the camps to keep grain beyond a week's ration. The overseers enforce the order, and Dòmhnall mac Raghnaill Maor signs it.
- **31 an Dàmhair, AE 79** — *Fish smuggled from Ros gharbh* (Ros gharbh). The fishermen of Ros gharbh carry salt fish up to the camps by night, past the Company's granary rule. The custodians' roll calls it the only trade of that decade that ran the right way.
- **29 an t-Samhain, AE 79** — *Catrìona goes to the silver town* (Muileann chiar — baile mèinne airgid). Turned out of Baile thais and refused work at every Company pit, Catrìona nic Eachainn goes east to Muileann chiar, and the silver guild takes her on as a refiner. The Company asks that she be sent back. The guild's answer was filed and has not survived.
- **3 an t-Sultain, AE 80** — *The springs at Muileann ruadh* (Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh). The Administration builds a new bath-house at the hot springs near Muileann ruadh for its officers mending from fevers. Dia-thìrich who had bathed there for centuries are let in on certain days, and charged a penny.
- **11 am Màrt, AE 81** — *Muileann chiar grows* (Muileann chiar — baile mèinne airgid). The silver town grows beside the coal workings, for the humans want both, and the digging goes faster than the old reverence would ever have allowed.
- **7 an t-Iuchar, AE 82** — *A second Muileann chiar* (Muileann chiar). The silver trade crowds the old town, and the guild founds a daughter settlement to the west for its refiners and carters, which takes the same name. The rolls call them the old town and the new, and do not always say which they mean.
- **8 an t-Ògmhios, AE 83** — *Silver for marks* (Muileann chiar). The silver guild begins to sell bar silver to the Company for marks, at a price the guild sets. It is the only ware on Dia-thìr in this age priced by Dia-thìrich hands, and the guild's hall fills with human coin.
- **28 an Dùbhlachd, AE 84** — *Silversmiths at Muileann bhàn* (Muileann bhàn). Silversmiths settle at Muileann bhàn on the road to the silver town and live by working the guild's bar into ornaments for the humans' market. Theirs is the one Dia-thìrich craft sold in an Tìr Thall under a Dia-thìrich name.
- **24 an Gearran, AE 85** — *Macha's priests bless the coin* (Cathair dhearg). At Tolley's asking the priests of Òrd Mhacha at Cathair dhearg, the order of the capital and the crown, bless the Residency's new coin. The priesthood of Macha teaches that the two horses of her rite, Dubh Sainglenn the black and Liath Macha the grey, each have their due; the dissenting priests say the coin is only one of them.
- **2 an Dàmhair, AE 86** — *The second change of coin*. The barter goods of the Dia-thìrich are marked down against the humans' coin a second time, on terms the humans' Administration alone sets.
- **31 an Dàmhair, AE 86** — *Wool marked down at Baile Mòr fhionn* (Baile Mòr fhionn). At Baile Mòr fhionn, where wool had been the measure of every bargain, a fleece is now worth by the Residency's table what a half-fleece was worth before. The town's weavers stop bringing wool to market and send it over the sea on their own account, until the Company refuses them freight.
- **2 an Gearran, AE 87** — *The boats of Caol fhiadhaich sold* (Caol fhiadhaich). The fishing fleet of Caol fhiadhaich, unable to pay the new harbour dues in marks, sells half its boats to the Company. The men who sailed them go into the pits under the next year's contracts.
- **25 am Màrt, AE 87** — *The dissenters go to Cnoc bheag* (Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag). Priests of Macha who refused the blessing leave the capital's temple and settle in the sacred forest at Cnoc bheag. There they keep the older reading of Macha's two horses, and take in custodians who have lost their seats.
- **23 an Giblean, AE 87** — *Iain Maor* (Muileann chrom). Dòmhnall mac Raghnaill Maor dies, and his son Iain takes the overseer's staff. Iain Maor is the first overseer schooled at the Mission; he keeps his reports in the humans' tongue and his household in Dia-thìris.
- **4 am Faoilleach, AE 88** — *The Levy* (Ros dhomhain). Tolley issues an ordinance, the Levy, by which every farming village in the west and north must send one in five of its able grown folk to the pits for two years. The villages are paid in marks, at the new rate.
- **3 am Màrt, AE 88** — *Levy officers at Caol mhòr* (Caol mhòr). The Levy's officers take their first tally at Caol mhòr in the north-west, reading the names of the chosen from a list in the humans' tongue. The custodians of the town write the names again in Dia-thìris, that they may know whom to look for.
- **6 an Dùbhlachd, AE 88** — *The Levy in the north-west* (Muileann àrsaidh). The Levy falls hardest on the villages about Baile chrom and the northern concession, which had never sent crews to the pits. The Dia-thìrich of the concession are taken; its human farmers are spared.
- **2 an t-Ògmhios, AE 89** — *Baile ìseal sends its people* (Baile ìseal). Baile ìseal sends forty-one of its people to the pits under the Levy, and nineteen come back when their term ends. The custodians' roll names the other twenty-two and the camps they were sent to.
- **6 an Dùbhlachd, AE 89** — *Muileann naomh buys its way out* (Muileann naomh). The custodians of Muileann naomh pay the Levy's officers in silver to halve the town's tally. The officers take the silver and the whole tally. The complaint is lodged at the Residency and filed.
- **14 an Dùbhlachd, AE 89** — *The druid school's hall shut* (Dùn thais). George Tolley shuts the hall of the druid school at Dùn thais over a lecture on whether the humans' blindness to the coal's colour is a kind of sickness. The masters go on teaching in their own houses, to smaller rooms each year.
- **30 an Giblean, AE 90** — *The last disputation at Doire chiar* (Doire chiar). At Doire chiar, a village of the druid schools north of the eastern workings, the masters hold the last open disputation of the school on the eve of Bealltainn, in the open air on the village threshing-floor. Its matter is whether a question may be forbidden. The Administration's clerk who attends writes that it may.
- **15 an t-Ògmhios, AE 90** — *Teaching in the sacred forest* (Coille Naomh Muileann chiar). Druid masters who may no longer teach in a hall begin to teach under the trees in the sacred forest of Flidais near Muileann chiar, where the Administration has no building to shut.
- **14 an t-Iuchar, AE 90** — *Building the last beacon at Baile chrom* (Taigh-solais Baile chrom). Work begins on the fifth and last beacon, on the north-western headland at Baile chrom, with masons taken by the Levy from the very villages whose fields they leave untilled.
- **27 an t-Ògmhios, AE 91** — *The masons of Cnoc thais* (Cnoc thais). The Levy takes the masons of Cnoc thais to build the beacon at Baile chrom. Their foreman, Dùghall Clachair, cuts the names of his crew into the lintel of the lamp-room, the only writing on any of the five towers.
- **26 an t-Iuchar, AE 91** — *The five beacons complete* (Taigh-solais Baile chrom). The ring of coast beacons is finished: Taigh-solais Baile chrom, Baile ìseal, Muileann bheag, Àth dhearg and Tobar dhearg. They serve a trade that is by now plunder in all but name.
- **24 an Lùnastal, AE 91** — *Cuan ruadh loses its trade* (Cuan ruadh). The ring of beacons finished, the Company's steamers round the island without putting in, and within a few years the old coasting trade of Cuan ruadh up and down the eastern shore dies.
- **22 an t-Sultain, AE 91** — *Taigh-solais Baile chrom lit* (Taigh-solais Baile chrom). The beacon at Baile chrom is lit with a coal flame, and the ring is whole. The Company's ships can now round the island by night, and the keepers' daybooks show the sailings doubled within a few years.
- **3 am Màrt, AE 94** — *Gorta Baile chrom*. The Great Hunger follows a failed harvest across thirty-four settlements, made worse because the Levy has taken so many to the pits that too few are left to till the land.
- **1 an Giblean, AE 94** — *Baile chrom goes hungry* (Baile chrom). The hunger is worst at Baile chrom itself, whose people could see the new beacon from their empty fields. The custodians write that more died there than anywhere else, and the Administration, which kept its own count, does not gainsay them.
- **22 an Cèitean, AE 94** — *The famine country* (Gorta Baile chrom). The custodians' roll draws the bounds of the famine country along the north-west shore and the hills behind it. Within them lie Baile chrom in its own shire; Ceann mhòr, Àth fhionn and Àth dhearg in the shire of Ceann mhòr; Muileann àrsaidh in the shire of Cnoc thais; and Achadh àrsaidh in the shire of Muileann àrsaidh. Thirty-four settlements are counted within the line, and the roll gives the dead of each.
- **30 an Giblean, AE 95** — *The hunger at Doire ghlas* (Doire ghlas). At Doire ghlas in the north the hunger takes the old and the very young first. The village sends its young folk to the camps for the Company's rations, and by the year's end it is half empty.
- **29 an Cèitean, AE 95** — *Inis mhin eats its seed* (Inis mhin). In the second winter of the hunger the townsfolk of Inis mhin on the north coast eat their seed corn. The Mission kitchen at the harbour feeds three hundred a day for a season.
- **7 an t-Samhain, AE 96** — *The hunger reaches Seann Bhrenn* (Seann Bhrenn). The hunger reaches as far east as Seann Bhrenn, where the custodians open the old grain-pits of the Holy Age, unfilled in living memory. They hold only dust.
- **6 an Dùbhlachd, AE 96** — *The relief ship* (Ros dhomhain). A relief ship with grain from an Tìr Thall lies a month at Ros dhomhain while the Residency and the Company dispute who shall pay for its unloading. Meanwhile the Mission opens kitchens at Cathair gheal and Baile chrom, and Anne Colby, come back to the island, keeps the one at Baile chrom.
- **20 an Gearran, AE 97** — *The Levy set aside* (Baile chrom). The Levy is set aside in the famine districts, too late for the harvest. It is not repealed. The custodians note that it was never used again, nor needed to be, for the villages had learned what it meant.
- **17 an Lùnastal, AE 97** — *Cnoc mhòr walks south* (Cnoc mhòr). Rather than starve, the families of Cnoc mhòr in the north walk south to the camps and take work under the Company. Their village stands empty for a generation.
- **9 an Dàmhair, AE 98** — *Robert Haskins Commissioner* (Ros dhomhain). George Tolley retires with honours. Robert Haskins, who follows him, orders that the custodians' council be consulted on the tithe, and then sets the tithe before the council has met.
- **7 an t-Samhain, AE 98** — *Customs at Seann Dunn* (Seann Dunn). Haskins opens a customs house at Seann Dunn on the eastern coast, and a Company store with it. The store sells the east its seed and its tools, and within a few years its ledgers hold the debts of half the district.
- **4 am Faoilleach, AE 99** — *The first petition*. For the first time the custodians of the Dia-thìrich act together, and not settlement by settlement, and lay a written grievance before the humans' Administration. It is not answered.
- **3 am Màrt, AE 99** — *The gathering at Ceann àrsaidh* (Ceann àrsaidh). The petition was drawn up at Ceann àrsaidh by custodians of nineteen settlements, meeting for the first time as one body. Peigi Ghlas, custodian of Cill ghlas, carried it to the Residency and handed it to a clerk.
- **6 an Dùbhlachd, AE 99** — *Àth fhionn signs* (Àth fhionn). Ruairidh mac Thormoid, custodian of Àth fhionn in the south-east, is the eldest of those who signed the petition. He was born before the humans' coin was struck, and says so beside his name.
- **27 am Faoilleach, AE 101** — *Grievance first written*. From these years come the oldest writings of grievance among the Dia-thìrich that survive. No hand is yet raised in them; yet in them it is first written that something has gone wrong.
- **18 an t-Sultain, AE 101** — *Leabhar Baile thais* (Baile thais). The oldest of them is a book of complaints kept at Baile thais, set down by many hands over some years: wages, deaths, the granary, the stream at Doire mhòr. The custodians' copyists call it Leabhar Baile thais.
- **17 am Faoilleach, AE 102** — *The songs of Fearchar Bàrd* (Muileann dhearg). The poet Fearchar Bàrd, a breaker of coal at Muileann dhearg since boyhood, makes songs of the Levy and the famine, and they are sung in the camps. The overseers forbid them, and because they were forbidden several were written down.
- **23 an Dùbhlachd, AE 102** — *Songs at An Taigh-òsta Grianach* (An Taigh-òsta Grianach). The songs of Fearchar Bàrd are sung in the roadside houses of the east, and An Taigh-òsta Grianach becomes known for them. The Company's carters sing them too, the keeper writes, not always knowing what they sing.
- **15 an Gearran, AE 103** — *The Company's deep-water quay* (Ros dhomhain). The Company builds at Ros dhomhain a deep-water quay for the new iron steamships, which burn the island's own coal to carry it away. Fearchar Bàrd makes a song of that, the most quoted of all his songs.
- **20 an t-Samhain, AE 103** — *The deep quay at Ceann chaol* (Ceann chaol). A second deep-water quay is built at Ceann chaol in the south-east for the eastern coal. Its builders are brought from the coast, and the village of forty houses becomes a town of four hundred.
- **23 an t-Sultain, AE 104** — *Baile thais walls its pithead* (Baile thais). The Company rings the pithead at Baile thais with a stone wall and a gate, and pays a watchman to count who goes in. It is the first working on Dia-thìr walled against its own crews.
- **19 an Dùbhlachd, AE 104** — *Catrìona nic Eachainn dies at the silver town* (Baile thais). Catrìona nic Eachainn dies at Muileann chiar, a refiner of the silver guild to the end. The camp folk of Baile thais send men to her burying, and the Company docks each of them a day's pay.
- **4 an Giblean, AE 105** — *The quay fire* (Ros dhomhain). A fire starts in the Company's coal sheds at Ros dhomhain and burns three days, taking two streets of the harbour quarter with it. The Company's inquiry finds no cause; the harbour quarter's own account has several.
- **22 an t-Sultain, AE 105** — *The council without a high custodian* (Cathair dhearg). After the death of the last high custodian the Council of Custodians cannot agree on another, and sits for years with the seat empty. Robert Haskins writes to an Tìr Thall that this makes the council easier to deal with.
- **25 an Lùnastal, AE 106** — *Tiormachd Achadh shean*. The Long Drought lies on the island's dry season three years together, and bears hard on a people already worn thin by the tallies of the pits.
- **28 an t-Ògmhios, AE 107** — *The wells of Achadh shean* (Achadh shean). At Achadh shean, whose name the drought bears, the wells fail in the second summer, and the cattle are driven west in a column the roll calls a day long. Fewer than half reach water.
- **27 an t-Iuchar, AE 107** — *The dry country* (Tiormachd Achadh shean). The custodians' roll counts ten districts of the east as drought country, worst at Achadh shean, Àth uaine, Achadh àrsaidh and Muileann chiar, and reaching down to Cuan ruadh and west toward Baile chaol. The Administration keeps no count of its own.
